confirmed: Source identity and version are correct: Martin Disley and Murad Khan, Designing cognitive friction with concept suppression in large language models, Human-Computer Interaction, journal version published online 21 Sep 2026, DOI 10.1080/07370024.2026.2708617; received 3 February 2026, revised 7 July 2026, accepted 11 July 2026 (PDF pp. 1-2). The PDF has 43 pages, including its cover and printed article pages 1-42. The checker read the entire markdown conversion, including Sections 8.1-8.2.4 and all references, beyond the original form's stated PDF pp. 1-30 coverage.

The lab_rct design is supported by researcher-facilitated classroom and individual video sessions, with each person completing unaided, unmodified Llama3.2:3b, and Unlearning to Rest conditions in a random Latin-square order (PDF pp. 16-17, Sections 5.1-5.3). Each condition lasted 15 minutes and involved chair-design proto-concepts written as image-generation prompts (PDF p. 17, Section 5.3).

The explicit participant flow is 47 recruited, 38 completing all parts, and 37 analyzed after excluding User 44 for possible misunderstanding or response bias; 37 is a people count, below 50, not a count of ideas or ratings (PDF p. 16, Section 5.2). The same 37 people contributed all three conditions, not three independent samples of 37 (PDF p. 17, Section 5.3; PDF p. 20, Section 6.1 and Table 1). Neither the randomized total nor randomized arm counts are reported, so their null values are appropriate.

Unlearning to Rest uses meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct with concept and vocabulary pruning followed by repair finetuning (PDF p. 12, Section 4; PDF p. 14, Section 4.1.4). The two chat models ran locally through Ollama; generated images were shown only after ideation (PDF pp. 18-19, Sections 5.3.1 and 5.5).

The questionnaire uses a 21-point scale for NASA-TLX-like dimensions plus a single perceived-ownership item; the outcomes are participant self-reports, not scores of creative outputs (PDF p. 18, Section 5.4). The analysis uses repeated-measures ANOVAs and paired t-tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (PDF p. 19, Section 5.6).

All S1-O1 reported statistics match: Mental Demand means (SD), Llama 7.24 (3.90), Unlearning to Rest 10.19 (4.45), unaided 11.49 (3.80); N = 37; F = 12.62, df = 2, 72, p < .001, partial eta squared = 0.254; Llama versus Unlearning to Rest t = -3.29, pFDR = 0.0050, g = -0.697 (PDF p. 20, Tables 1-3; PDF p. 23, Section 6.1).

All S1-O2 reported statistics match: Effort means (SD), Llama 7.65 (4.63), Unlearning to Rest 10.76 (3.51), unaided 10.70 (3.36); N = 37; F = 7.95, df = 2, 72, p < .001, partial eta squared = 0.177; Llama versus Unlearning to Rest t = -3.74, pFDR = 0.0019, g = -0.749 (PDF p. 20, Tables 1-3; PDF p. 23, Section 6.1).

All S1-O3 reported statistics match: Ownership means (SD), Llama 6.38 (4.86), Unlearning to Rest 9.16 (4.96), unaided 11.49 (5.83); N = 37; F = 12.43, df = 2, 72, p < .001, partial eta squared = 0.251; Llama versus Unlearning to Rest t = -2.77, pFDR = 0.0132, g = -0.561; Unlearning to Rest versus unaided t = -2.47, pFDR = 0.0234, g = -0.425 (PDF p. 20, Tables 1-3; PDF p. 23, Section 6.1).

The one-line finding accurately describes higher self-reported mental demand (10.19 versus 7.24), effort (10.76 versus 7.65), and ownership (9.16 versus 6.38) with Unlearning to Rest than with unmodified Llama; it does not demonstrate higher output creativity (PDF p. 20, Tables 1-3; PDF p. 23, Section 6.1).

Eligibility core = no and context_class = none are correct. Random assignment is present, but no study combines that assignment with creativity or diversity scored on participants' outputs; has_randomized_people_study is therefore false under the checker brief's definition. Section 6.4 explicitly disclaims empirical analysis of activity outputs, and Section 7.8 says fixation, novelty and diversity were not operationalized (PDF pp. 28 and 35).

The output gallery contains 18 illustrative prompt/image examples, not scored creativity observations (PDF p. 28, Section 6.4). The included behavioral-validation appendix generates ten responses per prompt per model; these are model outputs, not additional people or another randomized people experiment (PDF p. 37, Section 8.2; PDF pp. 24-25, Tables 6-9).

This is an original mixed-methods experiment with model validation, not a synthesis; there are no pooled estimates or synthesis study counts to extract (PDF pp. 15-20, Sections 5-6.1; PDF p. 37, Section 8.2). The default synthesis fields are appropriate.

No commercial study involvement is declared: both author affiliations are universities, the disclosure reports no potential conflict of interest, and the named funders are academic organizations (PDF p. 2, affiliations; PDF p. 37, Disclosure statement and Funding).
summary: The randomized study analyzed 37 people but did not score creativity or diversity on their outputs; all recorded statistics match the PDF. Corrections concern the included appendix, population and recruitment wording, page locators, and omitted code URL.
